thread:
incident-bot: 🚨 ALERT: Spike detected - p99 latency for /v1/generate increased 4.8x in the last 3 minutes, error rate 5xx+timeouts up from 0.2% to 6.5%

Priya K: I'm on pager. seeing a surge in timeouts, paging SREs now. linking traces.

Marco D: I pushed the canary ~2m ago (canary: release/2026-03-15-rc5). rolling back if it's correlated.

Lina R: Confirmed. Canary shards show p95 went from 180ms -> 1.2s, p99 ~4.5s. Host-level CPU modest, but RT queues backlog.

Carlos M: I have traces that show long tail on tokenizer stage, many requests with seq_len > 4096. Could be model variant memory blowout on the canary runtime.

Priya K: Good catch. Any 5xx stack traces?

deploy-bot: deploy event: release/2026-03-15-rc5 -> started at 4501236600, 12 hosts updated, canary 3/12 complete.

Marco D: Rolling canary back to release/2026-03-14-stable now. Command: `kubectl -n inference set image deploy/inference runtime=release/2026-03-14-stable`

Lina R: Also enabling circuit-breaker on route `/v1/generate` to fail fast for >1s latency to reduce load. Patch: `route: /v1/generate; max_latency_ms: 1000; action: fail_fast`

Carlos M: Flipping fallback to smaller model variant (gptx-compact) for new requests to reduce memory pressure. `traffic-split: stable=80, fallback=20`

Priya K: Customer impact: roughly 8% of requests hit 5xx/timeouts based on last 5m window. Mostly chat sessions with long context. No SEV pages from customers yet but risk rising. Notifying success/sales.

incident-bot: PagerDuty: Priya K acknowledged the alert at 4501236805.

Marco D: Canaries are rolling back. K8s rollout status: 6/12->3/12 updated (rollback in progress). logs: 
```
Warning: failed to allocate KV cache entry - OOM fallback triggered
WARN runtime: slow tokenization (avg 420ms)
```

Lina R: After rollback + circuit-breaker + fallback, p95 down to 240ms, p99 down to 780ms, error rate now 1.4% (was 6.5%). Progressing.

Carlos M: I'm opening a quick postmortem ticket, but short-term mitigation checklist:
- finish rollback fully
- keep circuit-breaker for 30m
- keep fallback routing at 20% for 15m then step down
- capture heap dumps from canary hosts (if available)

Priya K: Agreed. Tagging oncall-next: Lina R will own in the next 30m, Marco stay for rollback confirmation.

Marco D: Rollback completed at 4501236940, all 12 hosts running release/2026-03-14-stable. Health checks OK.

Lina R: Telemetry shows errors continuing to drop. p99 now ~420ms. We'll hold on removing protections until 15m stable window.

Priya K: Customer comms: "We've identified a regression introduced by a recent canary deploy affecting a subset of generation requests. We've reverted that deploy and applied short-term throttles while we investigate. If you see degraded performance, try reducing context length; we're working on permanent fix." Send to trust-notify if stable window passes.

Carlos M: Root cause hypothesis: canary changed tokenizer batching strategy + runtime kernel selection that increased memory working set for long sequences -> intermittent OOM/backpressure -> queueing -> timeouts. Will repro in staging with long-context load.

Marco D: Action items:
- Marco: create revert PR notes + deploy tag (done)
- Lina: collect runtime traces + heap dumps (in progress)
- Carlos: reproduce in staging with seq_len>4096 load (in progress)
- Priya: follow-up postmortem + customer impact summary (assigning ticket)

Priya K: Handoff: Lina R will be primary for next 30m (oncall-next). If metrics regress again, escalate to SRE lead.

Lina R: Acknowledged. I'll post a short update in 10m with metrics snapshot. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

incident-bot: Incident channel created and incident timeline started.

Priya K: Thanks team. leaving channel in 35m if stable.

Marco D: Heads-up for postmortem: include canary rollout validation checklist and add an explicit long-context perf test to the CI matrix.

Lina R: 10m update: p99 380ms, error rate 0.9%, no new 5xx alerts. Continuing to monitor.

Priya K: Closing pager if stable for next 20m. Will draft customer note afterwards. :white_check_mark:
